slot.title: Matched grip and the full stroke
slot.lessonGoal: Hold the sticks in matched grip and play a relaxed full stroke that rebounds to its starting height.
objectives: Hold a drumstick in matched grip, with the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger
Describe a full stroke: the stick starts high, strikes the head, and rebounds to its starting height
Explain why letting the stick rebound keeps the hands relaxed

visuals.intent: A hand holding a drumstick in matched grip, seen so the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger is plain, for the Learner to copy.
The four moments of a full stroke in order, raised, striking, rebounding, and back at the starting height, so the Learner sees the stick come back up on its own.

lesson.title: Matched grip and the full stroke
lesson.lessonGoal: Hold the sticks in matched grip and play a relaxed full stroke that rebounds to its starting height.
objectives: Hold a drumstick in matched grip, with the fulcrum between the thumb and the index finger
Describe a full stroke: the stick starts high, strikes the head, and rebounds to its starting height
Explain why relaxing the hands lets the stick rebound

blocks.text: Imagine a drumstick poised above a drum, just before you strike. For your work toward playing “Iris,” a relaxed hold lets the stick bounce after the strike [1].

Matched grip means using the same hold in both hands. The fulcrum, the point the stick turns around, sits between your thumb and index finger [2]. At the fulcrum, your thumb lies along the stick, opposite your index finger’s first knuckle [3]. In this matched grip, your other fingers curl loosely around the stick rather than squeezing it [3].

sections.heading: A full stroke comes back up

blocks.text: Your wrist raises the stick high above the drum for a full stroke, a strike that ends where it began [3]. You send the stick down to strike the drum’s playing surface, then allow it to bounce naturally upward [4]. The stick moves smoothly from down to up, without stopping at the drum [4].

Your thumb and index finger stay in contact with the stick while your wrist and fingers remain relaxed [4]. Relaxing your fingers, hands, and arms lets the stick bounce rather than holding it back [1][2]. A full stroke is one smooth trip from high to the drum and back to the same height [3][4].

blocks.caption: The Course’s own schematic shows a stick moving down to the drum and back to its starting height.
blocks.alt: Four moments run left to right: Raised, Striking, Bouncing back, and Back at starting height. Arrows show the stick moving down to the drum and upward again, ending at its original height.
